finding.claim: The avatar endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL server-side. The only check is that the URL starts with "https://". There is no host or IP allowlist and no block on private, loopback or link-local addresses. axios follows redirects by default (up to 5), so an attacker-hosted HTTPS URL can redirect to http://internal or http://169.254.169.254. The response body size is returned to the caller, which gives a limited read oracle. Attackers can probe internal HTTPS services and use timing and size differences to map internal hosts.
finding.source: req.body.avatarUrl, the JSON body of POST /profile/avatar, supplied by any HTTP client

trace.note: only checks typeof string and startsWith('https://')
axios.get(url) with default redirect following and no host restrictions
response size (img.data.length) is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: The startsWith('https://') check is the only guard. It does not stop internal or private hosts such as https://internal.corp or https://127.0.0.1, and it does not stop DNS names that resolve to internal IPs. It also does not constrain redirect targets, because axios follows redirects to http:// URLs. There is no allowlist, no IP resolution check and no maxRedirects: 0.

verdict.guard_found: none (only a typeof string and startsWith('https://') scheme-prefix check at server.js:11; no auth middleware, host allowlist, IP check, or maxRedirects limit)
verdict.reason: server.js:10 takes req.body.avatarUrl from an unauthenticated POST, server.js:11 only checks the "https://" prefix, and server.js:14 fetches it with axios defaults (redirects followed, no host restrictions) and server.js:15 returns the byte length as an oracle.
